author: Andy
caption:
Joro-spider (Trichonephila clavata). This slightly venomous beauty is native to Asia, but don't worry, apparently they have been spreading throughout North America since 2010. 
#korea #gapyeong

author: Andy
caption:
Black-backed Dwarf-Kingfisher (Ceyx erithaca). This guy slept on the same branch each night. The vivid colors made him pop in the forest of greens.
#borneo #sabah #kinabatangan l

author: Andy
caption:
Female Borneo Anglehead Lizard (Gonocephalus borneensis). Endemic to the island of Borneo. These lizards are incredibly good looking.
#borneo #sabah #kinabatangan

author: Andy
caption:
Broad-handed carpenter bee (Xylocopa latipes). This big  bee kept returning back to this very stick in its territory zone. I had to set up and wait for the right timing to take the shot he was very skittish and would fly away every time I tried to snap a shot. Poor butterflies that got too close got the iron fist.
#borneo #danumvalley #sabah

author: Andy
caption:
Rusty Millepede (Trigoniulus corallinus) are essential for cleaning and composting the forest floors. They are found in the moist unerlaters of the jungle floor. I think I probably got several leeches while filming this. 
#borneo #sabah #danumvalley

author: Andy
caption:
Giant Spiny stick insect (Haaniella). Somehow saw this massive bug on the night hike. I looked at the weird looking "dead leaf" for a while until I recognized it as a living thing. The guide was blown away that I was able to spot one. All the insects in the rainforest are either masters at camouflage and/or highly bitey and venomous. 
#borneo #danumvalley #sabah

author: Andy
caption:
Huntsman spiders (Sparassidae). Another find on one of our fantastic night hikes. Always a startling experience because they just all of sudden just appear on the trail in front of you.
#borneo #kinabatangan #sabah

author: Andy
caption:
Green frog (Hylarana raniceps). Night hikes were great to spot these tree frogs. Easy to see with the glint in the large eyes.
#borneo #kinabatangan #sabah

author: Andy
caption:
Tiger Leech (Haemadipsa picta). With the heavy rains comes more leeches. They hang on leaves until they sense motion or heat signature. Leech management is not as fun as it sounds when you already have to look all around while trekking in the rainforest to avoid all the other hazards.
#borneo #danumvalley

author: Andy
caption:
Borneo Tiger Leech (Haemadipsa picta). These voracious & bloody thirsty leeches have heat-seeking sensors that are tuned into and sensitive to human body heat. They twitch around when they sense victims. Beth and I found 15 of the mofos between us and I missed two that drew some good blood on my calf and belly. Part of the adventure.
#borneo #danumvalley

author: Andy
caption:
Long-legged millipede, (Thereuopoda longicornis). Saw this huge millepede on our night hike. It was about 6inches long and menacing looking. The guide told us they are extremely fast ... Everyone got back pretty quick and we along our way. 
#borneo #kinabatangan #sabah

author: Andy
caption:
Pig-tailed macaque (Macaca nemestrina) with baby. Don't show the macaque monkeys your teeth and don't look them in the eye. They can be very aggressive. I think this one was egging me on to get closer. 
#borneo #kinabatangan #sabah

author: Andy
caption:
Crested hawk-eagle (Nisaetus cirrhatus). This guy just caught a rodent that was still squeaking when we spotted him. 
#borneo #kinabatangan #sabah #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption:
The Alpha male Proboscis monkey (Nasalis larvatus). The males are notoriously hard to photograph as they sit high above on overwatch for other males and jungle dangers. We got lucky this one was doing the rounds with his harem.
#borneo #sabah #kinabatangan

author: Andy
caption:
Blue-throated bee-eater (Merops viridis. Hard to get the colors without direct sunlight but the green and blues show fairly well. Very territorial birds. We would pass the same spot every day and he was there everytime. 
#borneo #sabah #kinabatangan #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption:
Blue-eared kingfisher (Alcedo meninting). We were very fortunate to see this kingfisher stalk a little fish then masterfully dive down and catch successfuly. Absolutely beautiful, vivid color
#sabah #kinabatangan #borneo #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Monitor lizards fighting over female along the Kitanbatangan riverside #borneo #sabah #kinabatangan

author: Andy
caption:
White-crowned shama (Copsychus stricklandii). Endemic bird of Borneo.taken just outside of our room on the river 
#borneo #sabah #kinabatangan #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption:
Bornean orangutan (Pongo pygmaeus) female with her 1 yr old baby. The tenderness of their interaction was incredible. The conservatory where we saw these orangutans rehabilitates until they can be reintroduced into the wild. We have been seeing them in the wild but they are pretty elusive to capture.
#borneo #kinabatangan #sabah

author: Andy
caption:
Greater Green Leafbird (Chloropsis sonnerati). Picrured is a male leafbird. The females don't have the black chest (their chests are yellow). They are yet another endangered species.
#borneo #sabah #kinabatangan #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption:
Borneo tractor millipede (Stenoniodes). Very cool looking millipede. This one was 3 inches long. Beth is outstanding at spotting the 'hidden' insects. 
#borneo #sabah #kinabatangan

author: Andy
caption:
Rhinoceros Hornbill (Buceros rhinoceros). This thing was huge. We got lucky to see this guy on the way back to the lodge. Not the best conditions for getting a clear shot but  good enough to show how beautiful it was. This Hornbill was likely ~36" long.
#borneo #sabah #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption:
Crested Serpent Eagle (Spilornis cheela). This guy was perched right outside of the Gomantong Caves waiting for the big juicy bats to take flight for their night hunt. Why work hard when you can work smart for your meals.
#borneo #sabah #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption:
Green Tree Dragon (Bronchocela cristatella) aka Borneo Blood Sucker. Very common lizard but very cool looking.

#gomantang #borneo #sabah

author: Andy
caption:
Female Proboscis monkey (Nasalis larvatus) with young offspring. Easy to spot with their beautiful contrasting colors to the jungle.

#borneo #sabah #kinbantanganriver

author: Andy
caption:
Hushe is the last town along the Kanday valley before the Karakorum range. The subjects in the photo are the father, niece and daughter of our friend and camp kitchen assistant Nasir.

author: Andy
caption:
The end of our adventure landed us in the Hushe Valley. A gorgeous scene of cedar forest, edelweiss, a million flowers I've never seen, along with the lower elevation and perfect weather. The town of Hushe is where we stamped out from the trail at the last checkpoint and dusted ourselves off in town. Absolutely perfect end to an amazing adventure. 

#pakistan  #karakorum

caption:
Glacial melt took out the last bridge along the final leg of our trek. One by one all porters , guides and trekkers needed to get across this alternate crossing. Glad we got past it with little fanfare.

#pakistan  #karakorum

author: Andy
caption:
One of the more challenging experiences of my life. The Gondogoro La, or GG La as the locals call it, was a spicy 2000ft fixed-line, icy with crampon ascent. Climbing in a peaceful silence and then hearing avalanche very close by in the pitch black of night is one hell of a motivator to get up to the summit ASAP. Following our celebration at the summit, we were quickly slapped back to reality that the ascent was the easy part. The descent was a harrowing 3000ft fixed-line, super steep drop down the mountain with icy ropes and falling rocks all along the way. The rest of the way back to camp was a brutal undulating and rocky trail over the Goodwin austin glacier. Camp looked like we transported to Switzerland down the edelweiss in the fields where we slept.

#pakistan #karakorum

www.cleatusandthewestvirginian.com

author: Andy
caption:
On our way to K2 Basecamp. Quite the slog. 53 miles of trekking through glacial baby heads on undulating terrain... And we are only 5 days in. This place is humbling. Raw adventure.
#karakorum #pakistan #baltoroglacier 

www.cleatusandthewestvirginian.com

author: Andy
caption: One of the more profound experiences I've had... Hundreds of thousands of Sandhill Cranes taking overnight positions in the safety of the Platte River directly in front of our bird blind. Fifteen hours in a 3 ' x 6' x 5' tall box in sub zero temps while listening to the ceasless cacaphony of clacking beaks all night in order to view these marvelous creatures was worth every sec. Just nothing like it. #audobonsociety #sandhillcrane #cranetrust #canonphotography #canonphotography #rowesantuary

author: Andy
caption: Last night in Turkey. Spending our time in Istanbul eating our way through the street food (fresh fish sandwiches, rice stuffed mussels, turkish delights). Huge country with treasures abound. We will be back. Now time for a good ole' scrub down at the local himmam. #suleymaniye #turkey #istanbul #cappadocia #rosevalley #pigeonvalley

author: Andy
caption: Couldn't have asked for a bettter spot to warm up Beths' tootsies after a little hiking in the mountains and into the valleys during a snowstorm. Not all Sorels created equal. This "cafe" (middle of nowhere) was carved out of the soft rock and the owner had a hot pot of mulled wine waiting for us. #turkey #cappadocia #rosevalley #cave

author: Andy
caption: Uchisar Castle is the highest point in Cappadocia. The pigeon houses (dwellings cut into the soft tuff stone) are now only used by farmers who collected the bird droppings for fertilizer. The farmers claim this is the sole reason the regional fruits are so sweet. Hard to dispute, the fruits are incredible here. #cappadocia #uchisar #turkey

author: Andy
caption: The Hagia Sofia was built in 537 AD. Initially a Greek Orthodox Christian cathedral, then later "adapted" into an Ottoman imperial mosque. The juxtaposition of Christian mosaics with Islamic overtones is truly a sight to behold. The central dome is so massive its dizzying to look at from below. #istanbul #turkey #hagiasophia

author: Andy
caption: As we walked over the Ankerbrua bridge on our way to grünerløkka, we noticed each corner had a  statue of a Nowgian fairytale hero. Pictured is the wonderous Per Gynt, a legendary deer hunter from Gudbrandsdalen.#norway🇳🇴 #oslo

author: Andy
caption: The view from Rheinbringen was pretty spectacular. After our hike up the mountain, Beth looked up some fun (or not so fun) facts about the hike in Summer. Apparently there is somba line of people that climb it when the weathers pleasant. We ran into only one other party of climbers on our hike. #lowseasontraveller #norway🇳🇴 #Lofoten #reinebringen

author: Andy
caption: Most of the waters we encountered in Lofoten archipelago were glassy and great for picking up the mirrored reflections. Coupled that with the fire in the sky and you get some great shots. #norway🇳🇴 #Lofoten #Henningsvær

author: Andy
caption: What does 2 hours of sunlight look like? This is about the apex of the sun above the horizon each day. The best part is it seems to hang there forever. #Henningsvær is a cute little fishing village with one of the best sun viewing locations in archipelago chain. Can't get enough of these views #norway🇳🇴 #Lofoten #sunset

author: Andy
caption: Last day in the #Lofoten archipelago,we decided to explore our way over to the sun side of the upper islands. #Henningsvær was our destination. The 1.5 hr drive took several as we kept pulling over to bask in the glorious perpetual sunset views. This place is ridiculous. #norway🇳🇴 #sunset

author: Andy
caption: Started the day off with a brisk pre-light hike up Rheinbringen. The path to the top was paved with solid stone steps. Apparently they hired a team of Nepali sherpas to set and i wish i had a tape measure. The rise was a consistent 8" the entire way. With the snow fall the previous night, our hike felt like a winter wonderland all the way to the top. The last steep section was not complete (no steps) so we carefully made our way up the ice. The view from the top was incredible. We were very lucky that the weather held to take this pic. When we got back to the car a snow storm hit the mountain. #reinebringen #lofotenislands

author: Andy
caption: And there goes the rest of my nights sleep. The marine biologist overseeing the trip caught the 3 humpbacks breaching in front of us and sent us the video. So cool to have 2 vantage points #lofotenopplevelser #norwaynature #norway🇳🇴 #humpbackwhale #orca

author: Andy
caption: That time the humpback whale came out of the blue on the edge of the herring army and almost ate us. I'm the one on the left pointing at the massive something-or-other deep below ... Beth is the one screaming through her snorkel. To add to the fun, a million herring starting jumping out of the water all around us to escape the whales maw.

author: Andy
caption: We made it to the Lofoten islands in the middle of the pitch black night (or so it felt like it at 8pm). We had no idea what wonders awaited us the following morning. We rented a cabin in #hamnøy and spent the short day exploring the nooks and crannies of the beautiful southern archipelago. We made it all the way down to the very tip, a town named Å (yep, the shortest town name ever), to watch the noon setting the sun. The best part of sunsets in the deep north in winter are the long, protracted sunsets ... just absolutely deep, colorful bliss. This place just bumped something off my top ten places one must visit. #lofoten #lofotenislands #norway🇳🇴 #shorttownnames #a

author: Andy
caption: First Day in Norway was incredible!  Beautiful icy landscapes, fishing boats and huts, Aurora Borealis, snorkeling with Orcas in the Barents sea, and almost getting swallowed whole by a humpback whale racing to trap a mouthful of herring.... i looked directly into its mouth as it came up below us ...so close its fins hit us. Terrifying, exhilarating, very lucky not to have gotten injured. #norway #lofotenopplevelser #orca #tromsoe #sørkjosen

author: Andy
caption: Finally got to visit my favorite artists hometown and museum. So much better than I imagined. You really get to see and feel the creative energy that exudes from his studio and thought processes in his research.

Happy world cheetah day 2018! Help generate awareness of the plight of Africa's most endangered big cat. 
#serengeti #eastafrica #cheetah #tanzania #endangeredspecies #worldcheetahday2018 #internationalcheetahday #nationalgeographic

author: Andy
caption: I reallllly love hieroglyphics. These are located in the tomb of Mereruka. He held numerous titles along with that of Vizier to Pharoh Teti which made him the most powerful person in Egypt after the king himself. The tomb was 20 ft below ground in a very claustrophobic space. #egypt #saqqara

author: Andy
caption: Another carving from Iduts tomb is the birthing of a hippopotamus.this is very rare in Egyptian carvings. I am still amazed at the condition of many of the remaining carvings after 4500 yrs ... blows me away to write that. #egypt #saqqara

author: Andy
caption: Incredle detailed carvings from the tomb of Idut, daughter of King Teti (2200-2400BC). The Egyptians were said to carve the legs off of cows while they were still alive prior to cooking. Fresh as it gets. #egypt #saqqara

author: Andy
caption: Queen Nebet was wife to Pharoh Unis, the ninth and last ruler of the Fifth Dynasty of Egypt. This false door marks a potential path to her tomb. Only the deceased can pass through these doors. They would survive in the afterlife by means of the offerings brought to the doors openings. #egypt #saqqara #doors

author: Andy
caption: The front door to Ali Ibn Abi Talib Mosque close to Bur Dubai Souq. #dubai #middleeast #doors #mosque

author: Andy
caption: View from the top of the highest building in the world. Burj Khalifa is 2723ft high from its base to its tippy top. To put that into perspective for my Bay Area people, that's 2.5x the height of the sales force building. The elevators run at 10 m/s (2 floors a second) and have handle bars. Our ears popped ... 5 times. #dubai #burjkhalifa #middleeast

author: Andy
caption: Loxodonta africana (aka African bush elephant). A tender moment between young elephant and its mother. Loved watching them in large groups in the wild. So gentle with their young ... very scary when provoked. #eastafrica #tanzania #serengeti #big5

author: Andy
caption: Cercopithecus lhoesti (aka L'Hoest's monkey). This monkey can only be found in the wild in the DRC, uganda, and Rwanda. They sleep sitting up or holding onto each other. #eastafrica #uganda #bwindi #primate

author: Andy
caption: Alopochen aegyptiaca (aka Egyptian goose). The ancient Egyptians revered these birds as sacred. The Egyptian goose also shows up in their artwork. #eastafrica #ngorongorocrater #tanzania #birds #birdwatching

author: Andy
caption: Team plantation outside of Bwindi. Was curious whether this was a house, a shed, outhouse. Probably the latter, but I like the pic none the less. #eastafrica #uganda #tea

author: Andy
caption: Lophaetus occipitalis (aka Long-crested eagle). This cool looking raptor eats mostly rodents and small birds. They tend to perch on a tree and wait until they spot their next meal. Love the hair. #eastafrica #uganda #queenelizabethpark #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Cool fungal growth on the fallen branches in Bwindi forest. Love the colors of the greens and oranges together. Couldnt find their names. Maybe some of mycologist friends can help identify? #eastafrica #uganda #fungus #mushrooms

author: Andy
caption: Zosterops senegalensis (aka African yellow white-eye). Cute little birds that are also tough to capture. Unique white eyes look cartoony in person. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Vidua macroura (aka Pin-tailed whydah). These little dandies are fairly aggressive to other birds encroaching on their turf. They fly at them while flicking that long tail making thenselves appear a bit larger. Napolean complex at work. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching #nationalgeographic #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Haliaeetus vocifer (aka African fish eagle). The females is the larger of the two with a wing span up to 8ft. They almost look like like bald eagles from afar. Massive birds. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching #queenelizabethpark #nationalgeographic #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: This beautiful door is probably centuries old. You can see the Arabic influence at the top. It should be a excerpt from the Quran #eastafrica #tanzania #zanzibarisland #doors

author: Andy
caption: The doors of Zanzibar tell a story. The more wealth and status, the more the elaborate the door carving. Some doors are centuries old. I think this one is a younger because of the Indian influence (brass spikes on the outside). The spikes were said to stop elephants from breaking down the doors. #eastafrica #tanzania #zanzibarisland #doors

author: Andy
caption: Colius striatus (aka Speckled mousebird). The mouse birds are fairly common birds that are very social (as you can see). They can be seen upside down and eating huge fruits while. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching

author: Andy
caption: Lamprotornis superbus (aka Superb Starling). These are the blackbirds of Africa. We saw them everywhere. Not shy either. They will get within lunch snatching distance without fear. #eastafrica #serengeti #tanzania #birds #birdwatching

author: Andy
caption: Monticola brevipes (aka Short-toed Rock-thrush). Good looking bird in Tarangire park spotted catching flys in mid-air acrobatics. #eastafrica #tarangire #birds #birdwatching #tanzania

author: Andy
caption: Ardeotis kori (aka Kori bustard). The male bustard is thought to be the largest animal capable of flight. These guys get be about half the size of male ostriches. #eastafrica #tanzania #birds #birdwatching

author: Andy
caption: Bostrychia hagedash (aka Hadeda ibis). We didn't really need an alarm clock while camping. These guys are super loud first thing in the morning and early evenings. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching

author: Andy
caption: Golden monkey eating berries in Volcanoes National Park near the Congo/Uganda/Rwanda borders. #eastafrica #rwanda #endangeredspecies #primate

author: Andy
caption: Cercopithecus kandti (aka Golden monkey). We went out of our way to see the Golden monkeys in Rwanda. Very happy we did. We saw a huge family of ~100 monkeys in the bamboo forest and nearby potatoes fields.  Dwindling habitat and recent wars have decimated this species and placed them firmly on the IUCN red list (Endangered). #eastafrica #primate #rwanda #endangeredspecies

author: Andy
caption: Corythornis cristatus (aka Malachite kingfisher). Vivid bright colors flying through the air. You simply can't miss seeing these little guys cross your path. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching #nationalgeographic #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Ceryle rudis (aka Pied kingfisher). Two pied kingfishers hunting in a pair along Lake Bunyonyi in Uganda. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching #nationalgeographic #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Crocodylus niloticus (aka Nile crocodile). We took a boat ride along lake Edward in Uganda and spotted this large (8-9ft) crocodile basking in the sun with his mouth open. They do this to allow birds and bugs clean their mouths. We witnessed another one devour a large Tilapia in a violent shore encounter. #eastafrica #uganda #queenelizabethpark #crocodile

author: Andy
caption: Wading through a sea of green tea. #uganda #tea #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: Lybius bidentatus (aka Double-toothed barbet). Very cool looking bird with a serrated looking beak. I heard what sounded like a purring cat in a fruit tree and spotted a pair. Amazing how many different beautiful birds you can see in Africa. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching #queenelizabethpark #nationalgeographic #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Ploceus cucullatus (aka spotted-backed weaver). They birds were amazing to watch weave their intricate nests. Usually a hundred or so in very specific trees. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching #queenelizabethpark #nationalgeographic #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Cinnyris erythrocercus (aka red-chested sunbird). Absolutely beautiful birds. Rather timid birds that are hard to frame in a nice scene. This male had a nest close by and I just had to position and wait for him to go after this blossom. #eastafrica #uganda #birds #birdwatching #nationalgeographic #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: The children of Uganda are super friendly and love waving and saying "Hello ... How are you?" at every opportunity. Their responses when we waved back and engaged were priceless. Pretty much universal across East Africa, but Uganda's children stood out. #eastafrica #uganda

author: Andy
caption: Two juvenille chimpanzees playing high in the treetops. We watched them rough house for 20 minutes praying they wouldn't fall. #chimpanzee #uganda #primate #eastafrica #endangeredspecies

author: Andy
caption: Gorilla beringei beringei (aka Mountain gorilla). Still can't believe we saw these creatures. They are huge yet gentle and graceful. We were able to spend an hour with the family. Unforgettable experience. #eastafrica #uganda #mountaingorilla #bwindi #primate #endangeredspecies #natgeoyourshot

author: Andy
caption: Wonderful fields of green tea plants at the edges of Queen Elizabeth Nation Park. Almost blew my knee out jumping onto the roof of our car. Not in my 20s anymore... #eastafrica #uganda #tea #queenelizabethpark

author: Andy
caption: Pan troglodytes (aka chimpanzee). We were on our way to the entrance to the park when we came across a landslide that closed everything down. No problem. After a quick call, our ranger hiked up the road and met us at the car. From there, we descended into the jungle starting our trek for the chimpanzees. We found them high in the trees feasting on seeds and fruits. We could also see their nests which they make daily. Very happy we found them. #eastafrica #chimpanzee #uganda #primate

author: Andy
caption: Cinnyris cupreus (aka Copper breasted sunbird). I was walking down a village path and found this female sunbird eating bugs in a beautiful bush of orange flowers. One of my favorite pictures so far from the trip. #eastafrica #queenelizabethpark #birds #sunbird #birdwatching #uganda #nationalgeographic #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Still looking for the name of this frog. He was very well camouflaged on the forest floor. The rangers were looking at me funny while taking pictures of a frog on a gorilla trek. #eastafrica #uganda #bwindi #frog

author: Andy
caption: Terpsiphone viridis (aka African paradise flycatcher). Another lucky encounter. I spotted this beauty just outside camp. It looked like a cartoon in front of me. Totally bizarre yet gorgeous bird. Took forever to identify since it's a rare one. #eastafrica #birds #uganda #bwindi

author: Andy
caption: Want a cheaper way to acquire materials for that new home. Fire your own bricks at the job site. This setup contains 9000 bricks and will be ready for use in a week or so after firing in the kiln structure (Tanuulu). 2-3 brick builders are needed to mix the soil/sand/clay and lots of water. #uganda #brick

author: Andy
caption: Can't get enough of the early morning colors on the animals in the #serengeti. This lonesome male was parked just outside our campground. #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: Sagittarius serpentarius (aka Secretarybird). My absolute favorite bird. These birds hunt in pairs, walking the Savannah grasses looking for snakes, little birds, lizards. They pick up rocks and smash the more difficult critters. Such a treat to watch them hunt and catch prey. #ngorongorocrater #eastafrica #birds

author: Andy
caption: Crocuta crocuta (aka Spotted hyena). We spotted an animal running ... no,  sprinting at full speed across the Savannah. To our surprise, it was a hyena running to barrel into a group of vultures that found the lions leftovers. I didn't know they could run at high speeds for long periods. #serengeti #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: The Ugandan Wilderness Association has been invaluable to the conservation of mountain gorillas. According to the 2010 census, the population was at a minimum of 400 gorillas. Rumors are strongly in favor of much higher numbers. Hoping the next census confirms. #mountaingorilla #bwindi #nationalgeographic

author: Andy
caption: Pelecanus onocrotalus (Aka Great white pelican). These pelicans are huge. You can see its plumage start to get pink from eating the algae in the salt lake. Eagles don't eat them because of their large size ... but the alligators love them. #manyara #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: Circaetus cinereus (aka Brown snake eagle). This eagle's diet consists primarily of snakes and has the ability to resist bites  from and eat venomous snakes with no impact. They lay only one egg per year. #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: Panthers leo (aka lion). These male lions can grow up to 550 lbs. Nothing messes with them on the plains. Sadly, the numbers of these beautiful creatures has declined by >40% since the 1990s. From what we saw, this is most likely due to dwindling habitats as the farms of humanity close them in. #serengeti #eastafrica #big5 #endangeredspecies

author: Andy
caption: Upupa africana (aka African Hoopoe). These beautiful birds have unique anti-predator nesting defenses. The brooding female starts to secrete a foul smelling liquid that covers their feathers and nest. We didn't get a chance to get a whiff of it but I'm sure it's pretty gnarly if it turns African predators around. #serengeti  #eastafrica #birds

author: Andy
caption: Adansonia digitata (aka Baobab) trees are unique living environments for a variety of animals. #tarangire #eastafrica #baobab

author: Andy
caption: The town of Mto wa Mbu (Mosquito River). Yep, my feet got mauled. There are 25 different banana varietals in this region. Our favorite was the red banana. It tasted like it had spices added and nice and sweet. #manyara #eastafrica #banana

author: Andy
caption: Giraffa camelopardalis tippelskirchii (aka Masai giraffe). Loved watching the giraffe in the wild. The males have the irregular shaped spots. #eastafrica #tarangire #giraffe

author: Andy
caption: Equus quagga (aka Zebra). Stunning creatures. You really get the full effect when you see a large herd of them close by the wildebeest. Why the stripes? Everything from easy identification amongst themselves, less attractive to biting insects, natural air conditioning, and motion dazzle (confuses or distracts prey) #tarangire #eastafrica #zebra

author: Andy
caption: Cheetah brothers hunting early in the cooler temperatures along the Serengeti savanna. #serengeti #eastafrica #cheetah #endangeredspecies #worldcheetahday2018 #internationalcheetahday

author: Andy
caption: Acinonyx jubatus (aka cheetah). One of the most impressive animals I have ever seen. Really the apex of hunting evolution. We kept seeing them from half a mile away under trees or on termite mounts. We got an early start this day and scored. #serengeti #eastafrica #cheetah #tanzania #endangeredspecies #worldcheetahday2018 #internationalcheetahday #nationalgeographic

author: Andy
caption: Panthera pardus (aka leopard). Super lucky to have caught this cat sleeping in a tree. #serengeti #big5 #eastafrica #tanzania #endangeredspecies

author: Andy
caption: Galerella sanguinea (aka slender mongoose). Caught this family a mongoose raiding a large termite mound in #tarangire #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: Ephippiorhynchus senegalensis (aka saddle-billed stork). This bird just doesn't look real. Its bill is so colorful and brilliant. Nature never fails to impress #manyara #eastafrica #birds

author: Andy
caption: Gyps Africanus (aka African white-backed vulture) fighting over the remains of a dead wildebeest. #tarangire #eastafrica #birds

author: Andy
caption: Merops variegatus (aka blue-breasted bee-eater). Very pretty bird and difficult to capture as they are constantly hunting for bugs #eastafrica #tarangire #birds

author: Andy
caption: Platelea Alba (African spoonbill) and Egretta ardesiaca (aka Black heron/egret). We watched the spoonbill search the water for food with its large bill. Meanwhile, several black herons were following nearby and spreading their wings around their heads. Apparently, it uses its wings to form a canopy when fishing. #manyara #eastafrica #birds #audubonsociety #nationalgeographic

author: Andy
caption: Varanus niloticus (aka Nile monitor lizard). We barely spotted this guy until he started digging along the waterline. He was about 4 ft. long and fast when he found critters in the weeds. #tarangire #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: Chlorocebus pygerythrus (aka Vervet monkey). We were confused initially about the second tail until mama repositioned in the tree. #tarangire #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: Up close and personal with this Cape Buffalo. He did not appreciate our proximity the slightest bit.  #lakemanyara #big5 #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: Syncerus caffer caffer (Cape Buffalo). These guys were everywhere, by the thousands. Pretty amazing to see up close. Don't be a fool and turn your back on them. We heard many stories of how dangerous they can be. Our drivers friend was paralyzed by one of them trying to help a client. #eastafrica #serengeti #big5

author: Andy
caption: Balearica regulorum (aka Grey crowned crane). I was expecting to only see these guys in Uganda, but delighted to see them in the #ngorongorocrater. #eastafrica #birds

author: Andy
caption: Bubo lacteus (aka African Milky Eagle Owl). So many hidden nuggets in the Serengeti. Often times people are so focused on the larger animals that they completely miss the wonders lurking in the treetops. #serengeti #eastafrica #birds

author: Andy
caption: Wish this was a roar, but I'll take a nice toothy yawn from a male lion any day. The male lions have it hard, they protect the their prides' domain while the females hunt for food all day. #big5 #eastafrica #serengeti #tanzania #endangeredspecies

author: Andy
caption: This lion braved the mid-day heat to swipe a quick gazelle snack. With the advent of an increased population of hyenas in the park, the cats have been forced to hunt in packs and rapidly take to the trees to safeguard their kills. #big5 #eastafrica #serengeti #tanzania #endangeredspecies

author: Andy
caption: Very fortunate to witness a black rhino in the wild. We only had a minute or so to take it all in before he faded off into the savanna. #ngorongorocrater is definitely a rare paradise on earth. #blackrhino #big5 #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: The hippos in #ngorongoro crater were much livelier than other parks. Hard to believe such a massive animal could move so fast in the water. Even relatively small movements made huge waves in the marsh. #eastafrica #tanzania #natgeoyourshot #nationalgeographic

author: Andy
caption: Extremely lucky to capture this secretive and hard to observe Caracal hunting early morning on the slopes of #ngorongoro. #caracal #eastafrica

author: Andy
caption: Playful cub taking it a bit too far. Mom communicated her dislike and nap resumed. #serengeti #eastafrica #lion #tanzania #endangeredspecies

author: Andy
caption: Happened upon a lion with her two cubs sunbathing under the shade of an acacia tree. So incredibly cute seeing them interact with their mother. #serengeti #eastafrica #tanzania #endangeredspecies #nationalgeographic

author: Andy
caption: The Maasai people are a Nilotic ethnic group inhabiting central and southern Kenya and northern Tanzania. Every seven years the elders perform circumcisions on the next group of men to be. After the circumcision, the boys go out into the bush for three months painting their faces in charcoal, wear black robes, and consuming hallucinogenic bark. They come back from the experience as men and new warriors. #eastafrica #tarangire #nationalgeographic

author: Andy
caption: Agapornis personatus (aka Yellow-collared Lovebirds). These colorful guys can be found aplenty in the holes of the Baobab trees. We could have watched these birds interact all day long, very playful and funny behavior. #eastafrica  #tarangire #birds #nationalgeographic #audubonsociety

author: Andy
caption: Coracias caudatus (aka Lilac-breasted Roller). Gorgeous birds everywhere in Africa, but these catch your eye every time. They are excellent hunters and are usually found in mating pairs. #eastafrica #tarangire #birds #audubonsociety #nationalgeographic

author: Andy
caption: Phacochoerus africanus (aka the common warthog). The are hyper vigilant and lightning fast when spooked. Loved finally catching a glimpse of them up close. #eastafrica #tarangire
